(Fort Lauderdale, Florida) | college = [[UCF Knights men's basketball|UCF]] (2022–2023) | draft_year = 2023 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 9 | draft_team = [[Utah Jazz]] | career_start = 2023 | years1 = {{nbay|2023|start}}–{{nbay|2025|end}} | team1 = [[Utah Jazz]] | years2 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2023]]–[[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025]] | team2 = →[[Salt Lake City Stars]] | years3 = {{nbay|2025|end}}–present | team3 = [[Memphis Grizzlies]] | highlights = * Second-team All-[[American Athletic Conference|AAC]] (2023) * AAC All-Freshman Team (2023) }} {{confused|Taeler Hendrix}} '''Taylor Thomas Hendricks''' (born November 22, 2003) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[UCF Knights men's basketball|UCF Knights]]. As a freshman, he was a Second-team All-AAC and AAC All-Freshman Team selection. He was a three-time [[Florida High School Athletic Association]] (FHSSA) champion. ==Early life== Hendricks grew up in [[Fort Lauderdale, Florida]] and initially attended [[NSU University School]].{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nba/draft/newsfeed/draft-risers-inside-ucf-forward-taylor-hendricks-ascension-into-stardom|title=Draft Risers: Inside UCF Forward Taylor Hendricks' Ascension into Stardom|first=Nick|last=Crain|website=[[SI.com]]|date=December 20, 2022|access-date=January 12, 2023}} The 2018–19 University team with, which included [[Vernon Carey Jr.]], [[Scottie Barnes]], Jace and [[Jett Howard]], successfully defended its [[FHSSA]] Class 5A State championship with a victory over [[Andrew Jackson High School (Jacksonville)|Andrew Jackson High School]], despite Carey being sidelined for the championship game.{{cite web|url=https://www.theledger.com/picture-gallery/news/local/2019/03/07/class-5a-final-university-72/66145967007/|title=Class 5A Final: University 72, Andrew Jackson 46|accessdate=February 4, 2023|date=March 16, 2019|work=[[The Ledger]]|author=}}{{cite web |last1=Lichtenstein |first1=Adam |title=University School — again with Carey sidelined — rolls to its second straight Class 5A state title |url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/highschool/basketball-boys/fl-sp-us-5a-sf-bhoops-20190307-story.html |website=[[Sun-Sentinel]] |accessdate=January 21, 2020 |date=March 7, 2019}} He transferred to [[Calvary Christian Academy (Florida)|Calvary Christian Academy]] after his sophomore year.{{cite web|url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/highschool/basketball-boys/fl-sp-hs-boys-basketball-preview-2020-20201215-tezilaicpbb6nec4funiws7nqm-story.html|title=Boys basketball preview: Stacked Calvary Christian seeks national stage (plus other teams to watch)|work=[[Sun-Sentinel]]|date=December 15, 2020|access-date=January 12, 2023}} Hendricks averaged 14.1 points, 9.1 rebounds, and 2.1 blocks per game during his junior season while Calvary Christian won the Florida 3A state championship. As a senior, he was named the [[Broward County]] Player of the Year after averaging 15.1 points and 8.2 rebounds per game as Calvary Christian repeated as state champions.{{cite web|url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/high-school/article257843053.html|title=Taylor Hendricks: Broward Boys' Basketball Player of the Year|work=[[Miami Herald]]|date=April 15, 2022|access-date=January 12, 2023}} Hendricks was rated a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and committed to playing college basketball for [[UCF Knights men's basketball|UCF]] over offers from the likes of [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]], [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]], [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami (Florida)]], [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU]], [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]], and [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]].{{cite web|url=https://basketballrecruiting.rivals.com/news/taylor-hendricks-focused-on-his-season|title=Taylor Hendricks focused on his season|first=Jamie|last=Shaw|website=[[Rivals.com]]|date=January 24, 2021|access-date=January 12, 2023}}{{cite web|url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/highschool/recruiting/fl-sp-hs-hendricks-ucf-20210320-uc3q7atarvetpedgb63eg7r744-story.html|title=Calvary Christian's Taylor and Tyler Hendricks commit to UCF|work=[[Sun-Sentinel]]|date=March 21, 2021|access-date=January 12, 2023}} His commitment made him the highest-ranked recruit in UCF history.{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/ucf/ucf-basketball/ucf-knights-taylor-hendricks|title=UCF’s Taylor Hendricks is as Good as Advertised|first=Jack|last=Edwards|website=[[SI.com]]|date=December 13, 2022|access-date=January 12, 2023}} ==College career== Hendricks entering his freshman season at UCF was not seen as an NBA prospect. He started as the Knights' starting power forward.{{cite web|url=https://ucf.rivals.com/news/taylor-hendricks-excited-to-make-his-college-debut|title=Taylor Hendricks excited to make his college debut|first=Brandon|last=Helwig|website=[[Rivals.com]]|date=November 2, 2022|access-date=January 12, 2023|archive-date=January 12, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230112165451/https://ucf.rivals.com/news/taylor-hendricks-excited-to-make-his-college-debut|url-status=dead}} On November 8, 2022, he opened the season with a 23-point, 2-steal and 3-block effort against [[2022–23 UNC Asheville Bulldogs men's basketball team|UNC Asheville]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401488666|title=Pember's 40, Abee's 3s in 2OT get UNC Asheville past UCF|accessdate=February 13, 2023|date=November 8, 2022|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}} He was named the [[American Athletic Conference]] (AAC) Rookie of the Week for a conference record four consecutive weeks (November 21 through December 12).{{cite web|url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/ucf-knights/os-sp-ucf-knights-basketball-taylor-hendricks-aac-johnny-dawkins-20221213-aqrddargt5a6jlsadwwgcpz6jy-story.html|title=Taylor Hendricks makes web|url=https://theamerican.org/news/2022/12/12/mens-basketball-memphis-davis-ucfs-hendricks-earn-weekly-honors.aspx|title=Memphis' Davis, UCF's Hendricks Earn Weekly Honors|accessdate=February 10, 2023|date=December 12, 2022|publisher=[[American Athletic Conference]]}} The only other player to win the American Athletic Conference Rookie of the Week award three weeks in a row was [[Austin Nichols (basketball)|Austin Nichols]].{{cite web|url=https://theamerican.org/news/2022/12/5/mens-basketball-temples-battle-ucf-hendricks-earn-weekly-honors.aspx|title=Temple's Battle, UCF's Hendricks January 16, 2023, he tied [[Jalen Duren]], [[Precious Achiuwa]] and [[Dedric Lawson]] for the conference single-season record.{{cite web|url=https://ucfknights.com/news/2023/1/16/mens-basketball-hendricks-earns-sixth-aac-rookie-of-the-week-honor.aspx|title=Hendricks Earns Sixth AAC Rookie of the Week Honor: Freshman Taylor 2023|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}} Hendricks was named to the All-AAC 2nd team and the All-Freshman team.{{cite web|url=http://theamerican.org/news/2023/3/8/the-american-announces-mens-basketball-honors.aspx|title=The American Announces Men's Basketball Honors|accessdate=March 8, 2023|date=March 8, 2023|publisher=[[American Athletic Conference]]}} Following the end of the season he entered the [[2023 NBA draft]] and signed with an agent, forgoing the remainder of his college eligibility.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/35917878/ucf-freshman-taylor-hendricks-declares-nba-draft|title=UCF freshman Taylor Hendricks declares for NBA draft|first=Jonathan|last=Givony|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=March 22, 2023|access-date=March 22, 2023}} ==Professional career== ===Utah Jazz (2023–2026)=== The [[Utah Jazz]] selected Hendricks with the ninth overall pick in the [[2023 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/taylor-hendricks-jazz-no-9-pick-2023-nba-draft|title=Taylor Hendricks: Meet the Jazz’s No. 9 pick in 2023 NBA Draft|last=Siegel|first=Brett|website=ClutchPoints|date=June 22, 2023|access-date=June 24, 2023}} Hendricks became the highest NBA draft pick, the first [[NBA draft lottery|lottery pick]], and the first [[Eligibility for the NBA draft|one-and-done]] player in UCF history.{{Cite web |date=June 22, 2023 |title=Taylor Hendricks Selected by Utah Jazz with Ninth Overall Pick in 2023 NBA Draft |url=https://ucfknights.com/news/2023/6/22/taylor-hendricks-selected-by-utah-jazz-with-ninth-overall-pick-in-2023-nba-draft.aspx |access-date=June 25, 2023 |website=UCF Athletics |language=en}} Hendricks scored a career-high 12 points against the [[2023–24 Sacramento Kings season|Sacramento Kings]] on December 16, 2023.{{Cite web |title=Taylor Hendricks, Utah Jazz, PF - 2023-24 Game Log - NBA |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/players/28955162/taylor-hendricks/game-log/ |access-date=December 21, 2023 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}} On March 2, he posted a career-high 13 rebounds against the [[2023–24 Miami Heat season|Miami Heat]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401585495|title=Butler scores 37 points, Heat top Jazz 126-120 for 10th win in last 13 games|accessdate=July 15, 2026|date=March 2, 2024|agency=[[Associated Press]]|publisher=[[ESPN]]}} On March 17, he posted his first NBA double-double with 10 rebounds and 15 points against the [[2023–24 Minnesota Timberwolves season|Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/jazzs-taylor-hendricks-tallies-first-double-double-in-loss/|title=Jazz's Taylor Hendricks: Tallies first double-double in loss|accessdate=July 15, 2026|date=March 17, 2024|publisher=[[CBS Sports]]}} Hendricks made 40 appearances (23 starts) for the Jazz in his rookie campaign, averaging 7.3 points, 4.6 rebounds, and 0.8 assists.{{Cite web|title=Taylor Hendricks 2023–24 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4684806/type/nba/year/2024|access-date=February 9, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} On October 28, 2024, Hendricks suffered a fractured right [[fibula]] and dislocated ankle in a game against the [[2024–25 Dallas Mavericks season|Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web | last=Quinn | first=Sam | title=Jazz forward Taylor Hendricks suffers gruesome non-contact injury, expected to miss rest of season, per report | website=CBS Sports | date=2024-10-29 | url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/jazz-forward-taylor-hendricks-suffers-gruesome-non-contact-injury-expected-to-miss-rest-of-season-per-report/ | access-date=2025-12-06}} The injury caused him to miss the remainder of the [[2024–25 NBA season]].{{Cite web |date=April 7, 2025 |author=Jared Koch|title=Jazz’s Taylor Hendricks Reveals Major Injury Update |url=https://www.si.com/nba/jazz/news/utah-jazz-taylor-hendricks-reveals-major-injury-update |access-date=June 17, 2025 |website=SI.com |language=en}} Hendricks made three starts for Utah prior to suffering the injury, logging averages of 4.7 points, 5.0 rebounds, and 0.7 assists.{{Cite web|title=Taylor Hendricks 2024–25 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4684806/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=February 9, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} Hendricks made 33 appearances (six starts) for the Jazz during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], averaging 4.9 points, 3.0 rebounds, and 0.7 assists.{{Cite web|title=Taylor Hendricks 2025–26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4684806/type/nba/year/2026|access-date=February 9, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} On December 7, 2025, he posted a career high 20 points against the [[2025–26 Oklahoma City Thunder season|Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401810218|title=Thunder improve to 23-1 with 15th straight victory, routing Jazz 131-101|accessdate=July 15, 2026|date=December 7, 2025|agency=[[Associated Press]]|publisher=[[ESPN]]}}{{cite web|url=https://www.blackandgoldbanneret.com/alumni/40689/knights-legend-taylor-hendricks-delivered-biggest-game-of-his-nba-career-for-jazz-this-past-sunday|title=Knights Legend Taylor Hendricks Delivered Biggest Game of his NBA Career for Jazz This Past Sunday|accessdate=July 15, 2026|date=December 12, 2025|author=Ferraro, Jake|publisher=[[SB Nation]]}} On December 23, he posted a new career-high 21 points against the [[2025–26 Memphis Grizzlies season|Memphis Grizzlies]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401810274|title=Santi Aldama scores a career-high 37 points, with 7 3-pointers, to lead the Grizzlies past the Jazz|accessdate=July 15, 2026|date=December 23, 2025|agency=[[Associated Press]]|publisher=[[ESPN]]}} ===Memphis Grizzlies (2026–present)=== On February 3, 2026, Hendricks, [[Kyle Anderson (basketball)|Kyle Anderson]], [[Walter Clayton Jr.]], [[Georges Niang]], and three first-round draft picks were traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in exchange for [[Jaren Jackson Jr.]], [[John Konchar]], [[Jock Landale]], and [[Vince Williams Jr.]]{{Cite web |title=Grizzlies acquire Walter Clayton Jr., Taylor Hendricks, Kyle Anderson, Georges Niang
